title: Donor Acquisition
disclaimer: Synthetic training document for an educational project. Not an official policy, report or donor record of any real organization.
content:
Donor acquisition is the process of finding and recruiting new supporters. A healthy fundraising programme needs a steady flow of new donors to replace those who lapse over time.

Effective donor acquisition strategies combine several channels. Digital campaigns on social media and search engines reach large audiences at a measurable cost. Face-to-face fundraising in public spaces is effective for recruiting monthly donors. Peer-to-peer fundraising lets existing supporters run challenges and invite friends and family to give. Corporate partnerships and workplace giving can introduce the cause to new audiences.

Emergency appeals often bring a spike of new donors. Teams should plan a follow-up journey so that emergency donors understand the long-term work of the organization and stay engaged after the crisis.

The key acquisition metric is cost per acquisition, which is the total campaign cost divided by the number of new donors recruited. It should be compared with the expected lifetime value of a donor, which depends on the average gift, giving frequency and retention.

A strong acquisition message is simple, urgent and specific. It explains the problem, shows how a gift makes a difference and gives one clear call to action. Testing different messages, images and landing pages with small audiences before a full launch reduces risk.

All acquisition activity must respect data protection rules. Only contact people who have given valid consent, and never buy or rent contact lists without verifying how the data was collected.
